Choose eps for DBSCAN: k-nearest-neighbor distance plot

Source: R/seg_cluster.R
seg_dbscan_eps.Rd

Computes the distance of each respondent to its \(k\)-th nearest neighbor (\(k\) = min_pts - 1), sorts these distances and plots them. The suitable value of eps for DBSCAN is located at the "knee" of the curve, where the distances start to increase sharply: respondents to the right of the knee are in sparse regions (noise). The knee is determined automatically as the point with the largest distance to the straight line between the first and the last point of the (normalized) curve.

Usage

seg_dbscan_eps(x, min_pts = NULL)

Arguments

x

The output of seg_prep_data() (recommended), or a data frame or numeric matrix with already prepared clustering variables (no missing values).

min_pts

Minimum number of respondents in the neighborhood of a core point (DBSCAN) or minimum cluster size (HDBSCAN). NULL (default) uses twice the number of clustering variables.

Value

A list with the elements eps (the suggested value), min_pts, knn (tibble with the sorted distances) and plot (ggplot object).

See also

Other clustering: predict.seg_cluster(), seg_agreement(), seg_as_cluster(), seg_cluster(), seg_cluster_density(), seg_cluster_fuzzy(), seg_cluster_hierarchical(), seg_cluster_hkmeans(), seg_cluster_model(), seg_cluster_partitioning(), seg_plot_centers(), seg_plot_cluster(), seg_plot_dend(), seg_plot_heatmap()

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("dbscan", quietly = TRUE)) {
  prep <- seg_prep_data(iris, vars = -Species, verbose = FALSE)
  seg_dbscan_eps(prep, min_pts = 8)$plot
}

# }
